claim: Rhythmic behaviors vary across individuals.
source: Rhythmic behaviors vary across individuals.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that frames the study's motivation.

claim: The leech heartbeat system has a bilaterally symmetric CPG that orchestrates two coordinations in the bilateral hearts with different intersegmental phase relations (Δϕ) and periodic side-to-side switches.
source: In the bilaterally symmetric leech heartbeat system, the CPG orchestrates two coordinations in the bilateral hearts with different intersegmental phase relations (Δϕ) and periodic side-to-side switches.
evidence: This describes the experimental system used in the study, supported by the authors' prior work and data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Population variability in the leech heartbeat system is large.
source: Population variability is large.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: The leech heartbeat system is precise within a coordination.
source: We show that the system is precise within a coordination
evidence: This is supported by cycle-to-cycle variability data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Differences in repetitions of a coordination contribute little to population output variability.
source: that differences in repetitions of a coordination contribute little to population output variability
evidence: This is supported by repetition variability analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: Differences between bilaterally homologous cells may contribute to some of the population output variability.
source: but that differences between bilaterally homologous cells may contribute to some of this variability.
evidence: This is supported by bilateral variability analysis shown in Figure 7.

claim: Much output variability is likely associated with genetic and life history differences among individuals.
source: Nevertheless, much output variability is likely associated with genetic and life history differences among individuals.
evidence: This is an inference based on the finding that other sources of variability (repetition, bilateral) do not fully account for population variability.

claim: Variability of Δϕ was similar at all levels in one coordination.
source: Variability of Δϕ were coordination-specific: similar at all levels in one
evidence: This refers to the synchronous coordination, as shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: Variability of Δϕ was significantly lower for the motor pattern than the CPG pattern in one coordination.
source: but significantly lower for the motor pattern than the CPG pattern in the other.
evidence: This refers to the peristaltic coordination, as shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: Mechanisms that transform CPG output to motor neurons may limit output variability in the motor pattern.
source: Mechanisms that transform CPG output to motor neurons may limit output variability in the motor pattern.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the observation that motor pattern variability is lower than CPG pattern variability in peristaltic coordination.

claim: Variability across individuals and across cell types in underlying intrinsic and synaptic properties is now viewed as a hallmark of neuronal networks, even those that produce stereotyped output.
source: Variability across individuals and across cell types in underlying intrinsic and synaptic properties is now viewed as a hallmark of neuronal networks, even those that produce stereotyped output.
evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Coordinated regulation of highly variable membrane and synaptic conductances permits constant network output both developmentally and homeostatically.
source: Indeed, the hunt is on to find the mechanisms and rules that permit constant network output through coordinated regulation, both developmentally and homeostatically, of highly variable membrane and synaptic conductances (Davis, 2013; Marder et al., 2015; O'Leary et al., 2013, 2014; Ransdell et al., 2013; Schulz et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Network output across individuals is not very constant when looking at the literature more closely.
source: But how constant is network output across individuals? Not very seems to be the answer when looking at the literature more closely (e.g., locomotion in mice [Bellardita and Kiehn, 2015] and zebrafish [Masino and Fetcho, 2005; Wiggin et al., 2014]; food processing in crabs [Hamood et al., 2015; Hamood and Marder, 2015; Yarger and Stein, 2015], crawling in fly larvae [Pulver et al., 2015]).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies showing variability in motor output.

claim: Central pattern generating networks of invertebrates have provided some of the best evidence supporting the notion of constant output with underlying variability of conductances.
source: The central pattern generating networks of invertebrates have provided some of the best evidence supporting the notion of constant output with underlying variability of conductances (Goaillard et al., 2009; Marder et al., 2015; Prinz et al., 2004; Ransdell et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Phase of firing of component neurons is considered a critical aspect of a functional motor pattern.
source: Here phase of firing of component neurons is considered a critical aspect of a functional motor pattern
evidence: This is a statement of the authors' analytical approach, based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: Phase is by no means constant in central pattern generating networks.
source: and phase is by no means constant.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work in the stomatogastric nervous system and leech heartbeat system.

claim: Phase varies considerably across animals in the stomatogastric nervous system and in the leech heartbeat system.
source: Even though it is not correlated with period, phase varies considerably across animals as shown in the stomatogastric nervous system (STNS) and in our work on the leech heartbeat system (Bucher et al., 2005; Norris et al., 2006; Norris et al., 2007b; Wenning et al., 2004a, 2004b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Each animal arrives at a unique solution to producing a functional heartbeat motor pattern based on phase differences in the premotor pattern and synaptic strength patterns from the CPG to motor neurons.
source: Indeed, we were forced to the conclusion that each animal arrives at a unique solution to producing a functional heartbeat motor pattern; based on phase differences in the premotor pattern and synaptic strength patterns from the central pattern generator (CPG) to motor neurons (Norris et al., 2011; Wright and Calabrese, 2011b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work by the authors.

claim: Not only are underlying conductances variable but activity itself is variable in neuronal networks.
source: Thus, not only are underlying conductances variable but activity itself is variable
evidence: This is an inference based on the authors' prior work and the literature.

claim: Any attempt to elucidate mechanisms of regulation must consider what the target limits for regulation are, what are the sources of variability in network output, and how variability at one level in a network influences the variability on another.
source: and any attempt to elucidate mechanisms of regulation must consider what the target limits for regulation are ('What is good enough?'; Marder et al., 2006), what are the sources of variability in network output, and how variability at one level in a network influences the variability on another.
evidence: This is a statement of the research questions addressed in the study.

claim: All relevant neurons of the CPG and motor neurons in the leech heartbeat system are identified and easily recorded.
source: Leech heartbeat presents an amenable system for answering these questions because all relevant neurons of the CPG and motor neurons are identified and easily recorded
evidence: This is supported by the authors' prior work and the literature on the leech heartbeat system.

claim: The motor plant (hearts) in the leech heartbeat system can be directly monitored.
source: and the motor plant (here the hearts) also can be directly monitored (recent review: Calabrese et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review article.

claim: The leech heartbeat system is strictly feedforward from CPG to motor neurons to heart muscle.
source: Moreover, the system is strictly feedforward – CPG to motor neurons, to heart muscle –
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The leech heartbeat system's elements are bilaterally symmetrical.
source: its elements are bilaterally symmetrical
evidence: This is supported by the anatomical description and Figure 1.

claim: The leech heartbeat system operates without phasic sensory feedback.
source: it operates without phasic sensory feedback (Calabrese, 1977; Calabrese, 1979)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The leech heartbeat system has been demonstrated to be highly variable in output across individuals at each level.
source: and it has already been demonstrated to be highly variable in output across individuals at each level.
evidence: This is supported by the authors' prior work.

claim: The coordination of the CPG, motor neurons, and hearts differs at any given time on the two sides in the leech heartbeat system – rear-to-front peristaltic versus synchronous – with periodic switches in coordination between sides.
source: A unique aspect to this system is that the coordination of the CPG, motor neurons, and hearts differs at any given time on the two sides – rear-to-front peristaltic versus synchronous – with periodic switches in coordination between sides (Norris et al., 2006; Norris et al., 2007b; Wenning et al., 2004a; Wenning et al., 2014; Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work and by Figure 1 and supplementary materials.

claim: While rhythmic circuit output is continuous in the leech heartbeat system, it presents episodic coordination states on each body side.
source: Thus, while rhythmic circuit output is continuous, it presents episodic coordination states on each body side.
evidence: This is a description of the system's behavior, supported by the data presented.

claim: Medicinal leeches have two bilateral heart tubes which run the entire length of the animal.
source: Medicinal leeches have two bilateral heart tubes which run the entire length of the animal (Maranto and Calabrese, 1984a, 1984b; Thompson and Stent, 1976a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior anatomical studies.

claim: Segmental heart (HE) motor neurons innervate the hearts along their length, timing and coordinating their constrictions.
source: Segmental heart (HE) motor neurons innervate the hearts along their length, timing and coordinating their constrictions.
evidence: This is supported by the anatomical description and prior work.

claim: The HE motor neurons are controlled by a heartbeat CPG that produces a bilaterally asymmetric activity pattern.
source: The HE motor neurons are controlled by a heartbeat CPG that produces a bilaterally asymmetric activity pattern (Calabrese, 1977).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: On one side, CPG premotor interneurons fire bursts in a peristaltic rear-to-front progression and in near synchrony on the other.
source: On one side, CPG premotor interneurons fire bursts in a peristaltic rear-to-front progression and in near synchrony on the other.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2 and prior work.

claim: Motor neurons fire correspondingly to the CPG pattern leading to peristaltic and synchronous motor patterns, in turn leading to an asymmetric beat pattern of the hearts.
source: Motor neurons fire correspondingly leading to peristaltic and synchronous motor patterns, in turn leading to an asymmetric beat pattern of the hearts (Wenning et al., 2004a, 2004b).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work and data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The beat period in leeches is about 4.5 to 11 s.
source: The beat period in leeches is about 4.5 to 11 s
evidence: This is a measurement from the data.

claim: The beat period in leeches translates into several thousand heartbeats per day.
source: which translates into several thousand heartbeats per day.
evidence: This is a calculation based on the beat period.

claim: Embedded in the ongoing activity is the periodic alternation between the two coordinations about every 70–350 s creating episodes of coordination that span 15 to 60 beat cycles.
source: Embedded in this ongoing activity is the periodic alternation between the two coordinations about every 70–350 s creating episodes of coordination that span 15 to 60 beat cycles.
evidence: This is a measurement from the data.

claim: A switch cycle is defined as when a given side has completed both coordinations, one after the other.
source: We define a switch cycle of a given side when it has completed both coordinations, one after the other.
evidence: This is a definition provided by the authors.

claim: The core heartbeat CPG consists of 7 bilaterally paired segmental heart interneurons (HN) linked by inhibitory synapses and electrical coupling.
source: The core heartbeat CPG consists of 7 bilaterally paired segmental heart interneurons (HN) linked by inhibitory synapses and electrical coupling (Figure 1; review: Calabrese, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by Figure 1 and citation to a review article.

claim: Beat timing is determined by the mutually inhibitory bilateral pairs of interneurons in ganglion 3 (HN(R/L,3)) and ganglion 4 (HN(R/L,4)) linked by coordinating interneurons HN(R/L,1) and HN(R/L,2), which form a beat timing network and ensure bilaterally symmetrical timing.
source: Beat timing is determined by the mutually inhibitory bilateral pairs (Right/Left) of interneurons in ganglion 3 (HN(R/L,3)) and ganglion 4 (HN(R/L,4)) linked by coordinating interneurons HN(R/L,1) and HN(R/L,2), which form a beat timing network and ensure bilaterally symmetrical timing (Calabrese, 1977; Calabrese, 1979; Masino and Calabrese, 2002a, 2002b, 2002c).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Output to the segmental heart motor neurons, which occur in segments 3 to 18, is provided by inhibitory input from premotor interneurons.
source: Output to the segmental heart motor neurons, which occur in segments 3 to 18, is provided by inhibitory input from premotor interneurons.
evidence: This is supported by the anatomical description and prior work.

claim: Each HE motor neuron makes an excitatory connection to the ipsilateral heart section in its home segment.
source: Each HE motor neuron makes an excitatory connection to the ipsilateral heart section in its home segment.
evidence: This is supported by the anatomical description and prior work.

claim: The HN(R/L,5) interneurons switch the network.
source: The HN(R/L,5) interneurons switch the network.
evidence: This is supported by the description in the text and Figure 1.

claim: The switch interneuron on the synchronous side bursts with beat timing while the one on the peristaltic side is silent.
source: The switch interneuron on the synchronous side bursts with beat timing while the one on the peristaltic side is silent (Calabrese, 1977; Gramoll et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work and Figure 1.

claim: Switches in coordination occur when the silent switch interneuron starts to burst and the bursting switch interneuron simultaneously becomes silent.
source: Switches in coordination occur when the silent switch interneuron starts to burst and the bursting switch interneuron simultaneously becomes silent.
evidence: This is supported by the description in the text and Figure 1.

claim: Because the switch interneurons make bilateral connections to the middle premotor interneurons HN(6) and HN(7), phasing in these CPG premotor interneurons is dominated by the single active switch interneuron.
source: Because the switch interneurons make bilateral connections to the middle premotor interneurons HN(6) and HN(7), phasing in these CPG premotor interneurons is dominated by the single active switch interneuron (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by Figure 1 and the anatomical description.

claim: A single CPG consisting of bilateral homologous pairs of HN interneurons produces an asymmetric premotor pattern, motor pattern, and beat pattern that episodically and periodically switches between left synchronous/right peristaltic and left peristaltic/right synchronous states of coordination.
source: In summary, a single CPG consisting of bilateral homologous pairs of HN interneurons produces an asymmetric premotor pattern, motor pattern, and beat pattern that episodically and periodically switches between left synchronous/right peristaltic and left peristaltic/right synchronous states of coordination (Figure 2 A2, B2, C2).
evidence: This is supported by Figure 2 and the description in the text.

claim: The high phase variance in the CPG in peristaltic coordination did not translate into an equally high variance in the motor pattern.
source: Despite the feedforward nature of the leech heartbeat system – CPG, motor neurons, heart muscle – we found that the high phase variance in the CPG in peristaltic coordination did not translate into an equally high variance in the motor pattern (Figure 4 and Figure 5).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: The peristaltic phase difference that the HE(8) to HE(12) motor neurons achieve is significantly smaller than that of the premotor interneurons of the CPG.
source: The peristaltic phase difference that the HE(8) to HE(12) motor neurons achieve is significantly smaller than that of the premotor interneurons of the CPG (Figure 4 and Figure 5).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: The phase progression of the premotor bursting pattern determines the maximal phase range, but the segment-specific synaptic strength pattern, intrinsic properties, and coupling determines the phase realized between two motor neurons.
source: The phase progression of the premotor bursting pattern determines the maximal phase range, but the segment-specific synaptic strength pattern, intrinsic properties, and coupling determines the phase realized between two motor neurons (Wright and Calabrese, 2011b).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The premotor phase differences and the synaptic strength patterns interact so that the phase difference of the motor neurons progresses smoothly across the segments.
source: The premotor phase differences and the synaptic strength patterns interact so that the phase difference of the motor neurons progresses smoothly across the segments (Wright and Calabrese, 2011b)
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Smoothing and segment-to-segment attenuation of the CPG phase difference may limit the variance of intersegmental Δϕs, especially for nearby segments.
source: and this smoothing and segment-to-segment attenuation of the CPG phase difference may limit the variance of intersegmental Δϕs, especially for nearby segments.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the observation that motor pattern variability is lower than CPG pattern variability.

claim: When a larger or smaller number of segments intervene between motor neurons are assessed, then the variance in the motor pattern reflects more or less the corresponding variance of the CPG.
source: In support of this conclusion, we observed that when a larger or smaller number of segments intervene between motor neurons are assessed, then the variance in the motor pattern reflects more or less the corresponding variance of the CPG (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cycle-to-cycle variabilities in phase were low at all levels, in both coordination states, and on both sides.
source: We show that cycle-to-cycle variabilities in phase were low at all levels, in both coordination states, and on both sides.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Activity within an individual is precise.
source: Thus, activity within an individual is precise.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the low cycle-to-cycle variability shown in Figure 3.

claim: There is large variability in phase across individuals at each level.
source: We confirm and quantify the large variability in phase across individuals at each level
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: High variability at one level is not necessarily fed forward to the next.
source: and show that high variability at one level is not necessarily fed forward to the next.
evidence: This is supported by the observation that CPG variability is higher than motor pattern variability in peristaltic coordination (Figures 4 and 5).

claim: Repetitions of a coordination state have low variability and thus contribute little to population variability.
source: We show that repetitions of a coordination state have low variability and thus contribute little.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6.

claim: When the same motor act is performed by bilaterally homologous neurons and muscles, variability can be as large as in the population itself depending on the level and coordination.
source: On the other hand, we show that when the same motor act is performed by bilaterally homologous neurons and muscles, variability can be as large as in the population itself depending on the level and coordination.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Cycle-to-cycle variability within individuals reflects imprecision in the underlying neuronal networks and muscles.
source: Cycle-to-cycle variability within individuals reflects imprecision in the underlying neuronal networks and muscles.
evidence: This is a general statement based on knowledge of biological systems.

claim: Cycle-to-cycle variability is thought to arise principally from the stochastic nature of all biochemical processes, particularly ion channels, synaptic release, and neuromuscular systems.
source: This variability is thought to arise principally from the stochastic nature of all biochemical processes, particularly ion channels, synaptic release, and neuromuscular systems (Marder and Calabrese, 1996; O'Leary et al., 2014; Roffman et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: In leech heartbeat, the cycle-to-cycle variabilities of intersegmental phase differences (Δϕs) were small.
source: In leech heartbeat, the cycle-to-cycle variabilities of intersegmental phase differences (Δϕs) were small (Figure 3 and Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Across levels and in both coordinations, cycle-to-cycle variabilities were only slightly higher than that for the bilateral pair of HN(4) interneurons, which are part of the strongly, monosynaptically, and reciprocally interconnected timing network.
source: Across levels and in both coordinations they were only slightly higher than that for the bilateral pair of HN(4) interneurons, which are part of the strongly, monosynaptically, and reciprocally interconnected timing network (Figure 1, Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 1 and 3A.

claim: In the gastric pattern in the isolated crab STNS, cycle-to-cycle variabilities were substantially larger than those in the ongoing leech heartbeat CPG pattern and motor pattern.
source: In this episodic motor pattern, cycle-to-cycle variabilities were substantially larger than those in the ongoing leech heartbeat CPG pattern and motor pattern.
evidence: This is a comparison to data from the literature on the crab STNS.

claim: Cycle-to-cycle variance of Δϕ in the swim episodes of larval zebrafish seems also rather large judging from the representative example shown.
source: Cycle-to-cycle variance of Δϕ in the swim episodes of larval zebrafish seems also rather large judging from the representative example shown (Wiggin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an inference based on a cited figure from the literature.

claim: Many motor programs are shaped, and often stabilized, on a cycle-to-cycle basis by sensory feedback.
source: Many motor programs are shaped, and often stabilized, on a cycle-to-cycle basis by sensory feedback.
evidence: This is supported by citations to examples in the literature.

claim: Sensory feedback increases the variability within animals in the Aplysia feeding circuit, i.e., decreasing stereotypy, but decreases variability across animals so that a common solution space for functional output emerges.
source: Recording from two reporter motor neurons in the Aplysia feeding circuit, Cullins et al., 2015a found that sensory feedback increases the variability within animals, i.e., decreasing stereotypy, but decreases variability across animals so that a common solution space for functional output emerges (Cullins et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a specific study.

claim: The variability of individual motor components is negatively correlated with their importance in behavioral performance.
source: Intriguingly, the variability of individual motor components is negatively correlated with their importance in behavioral performance (Lu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a specific study.

claim: In leech heartbeat, the premotor HN interneurons on one side dictate a common relative timing (phase) of the premotor inputs to all ipsilateral heart motor neurons.
source: In leech heartbeat, the premotor HN interneurons on one side dictate a common relative timing (phase) of the premotor inputs to all ipsilateral heart motor neurons (Figure 1; Maranto and Calabrese, 1984a, 1984b; Norris et al., 2007a, 2007b).
evidence: This is supported by Figure 1 and citations to prior work.

claim: Any local sensory input to the CPG representing a segmental perturbation, if present, would affect all motor neurons.
source: Any local sensory input to the CPG representing a segmental perturbation, if present, would thus affect all motor neurons.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the anatomy and connectivity of the system.

claim: The recordings of the CPG and motor neurons are in the absence of any potential feedback.
source: Our recordings of the CPG and motor neurons are in the absence of any potential feedback.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental conditions.

claim: The period of leech heartbeat is modulated by a variety of inputs.
source: The period of leech heartbeat is modulated by a variety of inputs.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Period decreases with higher metabolic demand (e.g., locomotion) and higher temperatures, and increases in higher ambient oxygen.
source: Period decreases with higher metabolic demand (e.g., locomotion) and higher temperatures, and increases in higher ambient oxygen (Arbas and Calabrese, 1984, 1990; Davis, 1986).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In rhythmic behaviors, intersegmental phase differences do not correlate with cycle period.
source: At the same time, as in other rhythmic behaviors (e.g., lobster and crab STNS, Bucher et al. (2005); Hamood et al., 2015; crawling in larval Drosophila, Pulver et al. (2015); zebrafish swimming, Masino and Fetcho, 2005) intersegmental phase differences do not correlate with cycle period.
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: 'Phase constancy' as embodied in a lack of correlation between phase and period across animals should not be construed as suggesting that phase does not vary within individuals or indeed the lack of correlation of period and phase.
source: We emphasize that this 'phase constancy' as embodied in a lack of correlation between phase and period across animals should not be construed as suggesting that phase does not vary within individuals or indeed the lack of correlation of period and phase.
evidence: This is a clarification by the authors about the interpretation of their findings.

claim: In crabs, the phase relations across many gastric episodes across many days in the isolated STNS are significantly correlated with gastric frequency as seen from two individual examples.
source: In crabs, the phase relations across many gastric episodes across many days in the isolated STNS are significantly correlated with gastric frequency as seen from two individual examples (Hamood and Marder, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a specific study.

claim: In larval zebrafish, swimming occurs in episodes with declining cycle period.
source: In larval zebrafish, swimming occurs in episodes with declining cycle period (Masino and Fetcho, 2005)
evidence: This is supported by citation to a specific study.

claim: Larval zebrafish swimming is an ideal preparation to determine whether intersegmental phase delay scales with the cycle period in an individual episode.
source: making this preparation ideal to determine whether intersegmental phase delay scales with the cycle period in an individual episode.
evidence: This is a suggestion by the authors based on the characteristics of the zebrafish system.

claim: The population variability in the leech, at all levels, was about 2–3 times higher than the cycle-to-cycle variability.
source: The population variability in the leech, at all levels, was about 2–3 times higher than the cycle-to-cycle variability (Figure 3 and Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: In the pyloric pattern of the isolated STNS, variances were much lower within than across animals.
source: Similarly, in the pyloric pattern of the isolated STNS, variances were much lower within than across animals (Hamood et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a specific study.

claim: In the episodic gastric pattern, variances within animals, but again convolved across episodes across many days, were comparable to those across animals.
source: In the episodic gastric pattern, however, variances within animals, but again convolved across episodes across many days, were comparable to those across animals (Hamood et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a specific study.

claim: Variability increases when modulatory input is compromised (decentralization), in both the pyloric and the gastric pattern in the crab STNS.
source: Variability increases when modulatory input is compromised (decentralization), in both the pyloric and the gastric pattern in the crab STNS (Hamood and Marder, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a specific study.

claim: Variability in interlimb phase decreases sharply in galloping mice after ablating all V0 commissural interneurons resulting in a bounding gait.
source: In contrast, variability in interlimb phase decreases sharply in galloping mice after ablating all V0 commissural interneurons resulting in a bounding gait (Bellardita and Kiehn, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a specific study.

claim: Repetition variances were significantly lower than expected from the population variance across both coordinations and levels, and therefore seem not to contribute to the population variability.
source: Repetition variances were significantly lower than expected from the population variance across both coordinations and levels, and therefore seem not to contribute to the population variability (Figure 6 and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6.

claim: In much of the literature episodes within an animal and across animals are convolved making it not easy to determine whether repetition variability (i.e., inter-episode variability) contributes to population variability.
source: Because in much of the literature episodes within an animal and across animals are convolved it is not easy to determine whether repetition variability (i.e., inter-episode variability) contributes to population variability.
evidence: This is a critical observation by the authors about the literature.

claim: Interlimb phase variance in galloping mice was assessed convolving 51 episodes across three animals so the large variance shown probably reflects large repetition variance.
source: For example, interlimb phase variance in galloping mice was assessed convolving 51 episodes across three animals so the large variance shown probably reflects large repetition variance (Bellardita and Kiehn, 2015).
evidence: This is an inference based on a cited study.

claim: In a study on the motor and constriction patterns in fly larvae, covering forward and backward crawling, episodes and animals are convolved in the analysis presented, and the considerable inter-episode variability was not quantified.
source: Similarly, in an elegant study on the motor and constriction patterns in fly larvae, covering forward and backward crawling, episodes and animals are convolved in the analysis presented, and the considerable inter-episode variability was not quantified (Pulver et al., 2015) though it certainly exists (personal communication, Stefan Pulver).
evidence: This is based on citation to a study and personal communication.

claim: In zebrafish literature episodes and animals are convolved making it difficult to parse repetition variance and population variance.
source: In zebrafish literature again episodes and animals are convolved making it difficult to parse repetition variance and population variance (Masino and Fetcho, 2005; Wiggin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on citations to studies.

claim: Variability between homologous cells within an individual can also contribute to variability seen in a population.
source: Variability between homologous cells within an individual can also contribute to variability seen in a population.
evidence: This is a general statement supported by examples from the literature.

claim: In the crab heartbeat system, the five (presumably) homologous motor neurons – which are part of the CPG in this system – can express different levels of a common set of membrane conductances to achieve synchrony.
source: For example, in the crab heartbeat system, the five (presumably) homologous motor neurons – which are part of the CPG in this system – can express different levels of a common set of membrane conductances to achieve synchrony (Lane et al., 2016; Ransdell et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to specific studies.

claim: The crab heartbeat system seems more tightly regulated in phase than the leech heartbeat neuronal network, reflecting the synchronized rather than segment-specific nature of its motor output.
source: This system seems more tightly regulated in phase than the leech heartbeat neuronal network, reflecting the synchronized rather than segment-specific nature of its motor output.
evidence: This is a comparison and inference based on the characteristics of the two systems.

claim: In the leech, neurons arise from bilaterally paired columns of blast cells derived from bilateral pairs of stem cells (teloblasts) each of which arises from a symmetric division.
source: In the leech, neurons arise from bilaterally paired columns of blast cells derived from bilateral pairs of stem cells (teloblasts) each of which arises from a symmetric division.
evidence: This is supported by knowledge of leech development.

claim: Such symmetry in the origin of bilateral blast cells gives rises to the concept of bilaterally homologous structures and cells.
source: Such symmetry in the origin of bilateral blast cells gives rises to the concept of bilaterally homologous structures and cells.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on developmental biology.

claim: Blast cells differentiate into neurons, epithelia and muscles in each segment.
source: Blast cells differentiate into neurons, epithelia and muscles in each segment (Stent and Weisblat, 1985; Weisblat and Shankland, 1985).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work on leech development.

claim: There is evidence for stochastic events during leech development, for example the bilateral OP neuroblasts undergo symmetric divisions but for each the fate of the daughter cells is determined by position, and also in the formation of unpaired neurons, where either the left or the right neuron dies.
source: Yet, there is evidence for stochastic events during leech development, for example the bilateral OP neuroblasts undergo symmetric divisions but for each the fate of the daughter cells is determined by position, and also in the formation of unpaired neurons, where either the left or the right neuron dies (Blair et al., 1990; Stent and Weisblat, 1985; Weisblat and Shankland, 1985).
